gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-mandali: Mandali opens each e generously and keeps its strokes friendly. Under Balsamiq Sans, whose line never swells or tapers, a long paragraph would read as light and unhurried, like a plain sans should.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-manjari: Balsamiq Sans draws everything with the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel, no pinched curves anywhere. Then Manjari follows in a plain sans with wide, unclosed terminals, so the loud heading and the steady, approachable text sit comfortably together.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-meera-inimai: Meera Inimai reads like blueprint lettering, its open-ended curves given room to breathe. Balsamiq Sans brings the bold, expressive weight above it, and that gap between display and sans-serif text is what this pairing does best.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-metrophobic: Chunky, hand-cut and loud. Balsamiq Sans holds one stroke from top to baseline, while Metrophobic glides around each bend with a smooth, modern sans that stays out of its way.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-mina: Balsamiq Sans keeps the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel, with no tight, pinched curves anywhere in it. Mina's sans-serif text, with its unclosed small round letters, would read smoothly down a page.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-mingzat: Mingzat reads curvy and unclamped, a contemporary sans-serif with a relaxed hand. Balsamiq Sans does best as a bold, single-weight outline voice up top, while Mingzat is built for the quieter job of carrying the text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-moderustic: Moderustic looks like a broad nib left curves unfinished. Balsamiq Sans, monoline and bold, sits over that plain sans like a marker headline above softly open text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-molengo: Molengo reads crisply, its wide gaps keeping even tiny sizes sharp and its sans-serif manner quietly neutral. Balsamiq Sans is the loud one here, and that split between expressive and plain is the strongest thing about the pairing.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-momo-trust-sans: Marker-bold meets sturdy. Momo Trust Sans has bowls as heavy as its stems and wide, unclosed mouths on curved letters, so a long stretch of it feels solid, open and friendly beneath Balsamiq Sans.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-monda: Balsamiq Sans never varies between thick and thin, a single constant line that feels like stencil-cut channel. And Monda, a plain sans with unclogged small counters, leaves the heading to earn its keep big and short.
